scope: Complete all evidence-backed ordinary financial omissions and finite self-delegate roots at the18 positive existing router/financial-manager targets from routerAudit plus2 independently exact-source-bound currentactive iZumi manager/router roots found by the full-ABI-only follow-up audit, excluding already handled22 router wrappers, existing NPM exact8 wrappers, Pendle and V4 reserved wrapper models. Parent-requested extension adds ONLY standalone standard four-argument empty-data NFT transfer at the18 existing Uniswap/Sushi/Pancake NPM targets; their exact8 wrappers/children remain unchanged. No new protocol, chain, contract target, grant, profile or runtime-discovered ABI.

lineage.sourceRetention: Complete relevant root/inherited payment/NFT/init/dependency source bodies are retained by actual UTF-8 SHA256 in sourcePool. Every original full ABI/receipt/source inventory is additionally bound to its exact retained evidence-file SHA256 and JSON pointer; allCompilerInputSourceSha256 lists full input closure without promoting unused modules to deployed methods. SHA256 is source retention only, never function identity. Source match grades, constructor arguments, proxy/clone/library qualifications and mutable configuration remain actual recorded facts.
lineage.historicalSupersession: Only listed stale opaque-multicall/no-settlement-helper/transfer exclusions are superseded by concrete source-backed admission. Existing source files are historical receipts, not silently rewritten. Current catalog status supersedes stale inactive Ekubo family text; no inactive/withdrawal-only product is revived. Full-ABI-only follow-up supersedes the earlier routerAudit claim that iZumi selected inventories had no wrapper: exact sourceEvidence18/19 full ABIs and inherited Base body expose two concrete existing-target roots. This is no new protocol/target admission.

identityHashMethod.implementation: Actual repository exports functionAbiHash from src/modules/defi/registry/defi-manifest.ts and executionScopeHash from src/modules/defi/execution/scope.ts, called using node -r ts-node/register/transpile-only.
identityHashMethod.functionAbiHash: Keccak256 of recursively key-sorted JSON for [actualFunctionAbi], preserving array order and exact names/internalType; selected old children use their unchanged actual catalog fragment, newly admitted children and roots use exact retained per-target full ABI fragments.
identityHashMethod.emptyDataHash: Actual repository executionScopeHash for {kind:empty-callback-data-v1,bytesArgIndex:3} or index4, never SHA256. Hash REQUIRED iff allowed child has this scope; decoder must enforce exact canonical empty bytes. No other scoped child.

executionRestrictions: Finite same-target self-delegate batch only. Every requested child, including repeated children, needs its own active verified exact chain/target capability, actual ABI hash, grants and pause checks. Only listed plain children or listed empty-callback-data-v1 children with their actual scope hash are accepted; the existing empty-data decoder runs for each scoped child. No recursion, nested multicall, authority, permit, callback entrypoint or opaque executor. Canonical ABI, aggregate10-node/64KiB budget including root+every expanded child, shared operation/target accounting and final commitments remain enforced.

The outer caller and original native msg.value are preserved through every self-delegatecall; one transaction supplies native value once, not separately to each child. The actual native balance is shared and depleted by payments, wraps and refunds. Positive inherited value still makes any nonpayable child revert/reject even when the root is payable. No batch-only prefunding, per-child native allocation or blanket payable-to-nonpayable reinterpretation is claimed.

Native/ERC20 balances used by fixed refund/sweep/unwrap helpers are shared contract custody, not caller-attributed escrow. A helper may transfer the entire actual balance, including third-party surplus, to its source-selected caller or supplied recipient; it does not prove entitlement or prevent another caller recovering stranded funds. Amount minima and recipients remain financial parameters; fee helpers bound the gross balance, not net recipient receipts. Native recipient rejection or token behavior can revert. No automatic settlement/refund is inserted.

Every function remains separately grantable/pausable. Adding root or source evidence does not assign any grant, role, permit, token approval, NFT operator authorization or settlement recipient protection.

Preserve every old ID/ABI/scope/profile/fingerprint. same-target-multicall-v1 exact8 and same-target-router-multicall-v1 exact23 signature definitions remain unchanged. Elk2 newly added roots use the unchanged exact23 grammar; the other16 use new same-target-financial-multicall-v1 with complete eligible current+ordinary child closure.

Current active verified Ekubo Positions only. No stale inactive record or rejected withdrawal-only endpoint is revived. Timeswap targets have independent per-target finite vocabularies and source receipts, never cross-target delegation.

additions.label: iZumi LiquidityManager finite same-target financial multicall
additions.description: Exact direct Base sequential self-delegate batch closed over all source-backed current and new financial children, not a fallback/module executor.
warnings: Static exact-deployment ABI/source evidence only, not continuous runtime identity, current configuration, funding, allowance, liquidity, execution success or financial-safety assurance. Existing exact-function grants, pauses, canonical calldata, native-value and final commitment checks remain mandatory. No approval, permit, administrator, arbitrary executor, protocol, chain or target admission is added.

Finite same-target self-delegate batch only. Every requested child, including repeated children, needs its own active verified exact chain/target capability, actual ABI hash, grants and pause checks. Only listed plain children or listed empty-callback-data-v1 children with their actual scope hash are accepted; the existing empty-data decoder runs for each scoped child. No recursion, nested multicall, authority, permit, callback entrypoint or opaque executor. Canonical ABI, aggregate10-node/64KiB budget including root+every expanded child, shared operation/target accounting and final commitments remain enforced.

The outer caller and original native msg.value are preserved through every self-delegatecall; one transaction supplies native value once, not separately to each child. The actual native balance is shared and depleted by payments, wraps and refunds. Positive inherited value still makes any nonpayable child revert/reject even when the root is payable. No batch-only prefunding, per-child native allocation or blanket payable-to-nonpayable reinterpretation is claimed.

Native/ERC20 balances used by fixed refund/sweep/unwrap helpers are shared contract custody, not caller-attributed escrow. A helper may transfer the entire actual balance, including third-party surplus, to its source-selected caller or supplied recipient; it does not prove entitlement or prevent another caller recovering stranded funds. Amount minima and recipients remain financial parameters; fee helpers bound the gross balance, not net recipient receipts. Native recipient rejection or token behavior can revert. No automatic settlement/refund is inserted.

Atomic failure: child revert of fewer than68 bytes becomes empty revert; other data is offset by4 and decoded as Error(string). Arbitrary custom-error bytes are NOT preserved and may be transformed or fail string decoding.

inherit: exact Base.pay wraps only owed WETH9 amount when real address(this).balance suffices, otherwise transfers actual held token or pulls payer allowance. No msg.value credit ledger or repeated funding. Base refundETH transfers remaining native to original caller, sweepToken sends actual entire token balance after minimum, unwrapWETH9 withdraws actual entire WETH9 balance after minimum. Receive accepts ETH from any sender: shared custody is public surplus, not caller attribution. createPool/burn/decLiquidity and standard NFT transfers are intrinsically nonpayable; positive root value is rejected for any such child while payable mint/addLiquidity/collect/helpers can compose with the actual single funding. createPool only typed canonical factory lookup/newPool, not arbitrary executor; all current liquidity/NFT ownership controls remain.

Exact inherited Base self-delegate loop: original caller/value, atomic child failure; short revert becomes empty revert, otherwise Error(string) is decoded, so arbitrary custom-error bytes may transform or fail decoding. Direct exact-match nonproxy root, no fallback/module implementation dispatch in deployed source/ABI. Internal OZ Address delegatecall library utility does not itself create an externally callable module executor. Constructor fixes factory/WETH9 but this receipt does not retain concrete constructor immutable values/getter state; no fresh immutable/current-configuration attestation is asserted.

No batch-only prefunding, per-child native allocation or blanket payable-to-nonpayable reinterpretation is claimed.

Native/ERC20 balances used by fixed refund/sweep/unwrap helpers are shared contract custody, not caller-attributed escrow. A helper may transfer the entire actual balance, including third-party surplus, to its source-selected caller or supplied recipient; it does not prove entitlement or prevent another caller recovering stranded funds. Amount minima and recipients remain financial parameters; fee helpers bound the gross balance, not net recipient receipts. Native recipient rejection or token behavior can revert. No automatic settlement/refund is inserted.

Atomic failure: child revert of fewer than68 bytes becomes empty revert; other data is offset by4 and decoded as Error(string). Arbitrary custom-error bytes are NOT preserved and may be transformed or fail string decoding.

inherit: exact Base.pay wraps only owed WETH9 amount when real address(this).balance suffices, otherwise transfers actual held token or pulls payer allowance. No msg.value credit ledger or repeated funding. Base refundETH transfers remaining native to original caller, sweepToken sends actual entire token balance after minimum, unwrapWETH9 withdraws actual entire WETH9 balance after minimum. Receive accepts ETH from any sender: shared custody is public surplus, not caller attribution.

Exact inherited Base self-delegate loop: original caller/value, atomic child failure; short revert becomes empty revert, otherwise Error(string) is decoded, so arbitrary custom-error bytes may transform or fail decoding. Direct exact-match nonproxy root, no fallback/module implementation dispatch in deployed source/ABI. Internal OZ Address delegatecall library utility does not itself create an externally callable module executor. Constructor fixes factory/WETH9 but this receipt does not retain concrete constructor immutable values/getter state; no fresh immutable/current-configuration attestation is asserted.

Caller is fixed as payer. ERC20 input is pulled from msg.sender by router allowance in validated pool callback; no raw pool prefunding or standalone mint/burn is used. For ordinary token-funded swaps send zero native value and pre-establish needed input allowance. Catalog adds no approval/signature authority.

The original four selected swap ABI methods are payable but do not automatically refund unused ETH, unwrap WETH output or sweep assets. Native-funded exact-output swaps and nonzero price-limit partial fills can leave ETH/input residue publicly recoverable through the separately granted fixed refund/sweep methods. Do not overpay, prefund router, set recipient=zero/router, or assume a complete native-asset workflow; route output directly to intended nonzero recipient. Zero recipient deliberately redirects output into router custody. Token output to third parties is intentional recipient authority, not own-wallet protection.

exactInputSingle requests amountIn and enforces amountOut>=amountOutMinimum. A nonzero sqrtPriceLimitX96 can produce a partial input fill. exactOutputSingle enforces amountIn<=amountInMaximum; when sqrtPriceLimitX96=0 source also requires full amountOut, while a nonzero limit explicitly permits receiving less than requested output. Set limits intentionally; return values are respectively output received and input paid. No fee-on-transfer/rebasing-token compatibility or receiver delta guarantee is asserted.

Quantity fields use each token base units, deadline uses Unix seconds with block.timestamp<=deadline, sqrtPriceLimitX96 uses Q64.96, and tickSpacing is NOT a fee basis-point field. Zero price limit selects near-extreme allowed V3 price boundary. Pool swap math determines price impact, rounding and fees; use meaningful minimum-output/maximum-input, deadline and optional directional price bound. No fixed rate or fee is promised.

Fee-on-transfer variant uses swapWithPaymentInAdvance and checks returned pool output, not an independent recipient token balance.

Direct SwapRouter (not a proxy); verified constructor binds factory 0x10253594a832f967994b44f33411940533302acb, poolDeployer 0xd7cb0e0692f2d55a17ba81c1fe5501d66774fc4a and WNativeToken/WMON 0x3bd359c1119da7da1d913d1c4d2b7c461115433a. ETH-like payable value means native MON, not ETH.

Tokens, amounts, recipient, pool key/deployer, slippage and deadline are caller financial parameters. ERC20 inputs require allowance to this router. A nonzero intended recipient should be used: zero sends output to the router. Fixed sweep/unwrap/refund helpers and a finite financial multicall are now separately granted. These standalone swaps still do not automatically unwrap native output or recover residual native value.

Payment uses router native balance first when input is WMON and balance covers the callback; otherwise it pulls ERC20 from the payer. Overpayment and partial-fill native-input swaps can strand value; residual balance is publicly refundable by the separately granted fixed helper. Prefer WMON ERC20 input with zero native value for standalone calls; do not send unrelated value.

Path bytes are tokenA(20 bytes), custom deployer(20 bytes), tokenB(20 bytes), repeating deployer+token segments. Exact output reverses the path. Deployer is a financial pool-key salt component, not a call target: targets are CREATE2-derived under immutable poolDeployer and deployed init-code hash; callbacks verify that derivation. Source does not enforce exact path length, and trailing bytes may be ignored; no custom payload/aggregator execution is admitted.

Pool/plugin fees, liquidity and token transfer behavior determine outcomes. The fee-on-transfer variant calls swapWithPaymentInAdvance and compares pool-reported output, not necessarily recipient net taxed-token receipts. A nonzero exact-output single price limit permits less than requested output; source requires full output only with limitSqrtPrice zero.

Ethereum current v1 MetricOmmSimpleRouter only; nonproxy. Source reports Sourcify runtimeMatch=match and creationMatch=match, not exact_match. Registered Metric pool swaps only; externalSwap, sequence, permits and callbacks remain excluded; fixed public settlement helpers and a finite financial multicall are now separately granted.

Pool membership is checked against immutable factory and callback caller against transient expected pool plus factory. Payer is msg.sender on initial funding and router on intermediate hops. Output goes to caller-specified recipient. tokenIn/tokenOut and adjacent path token addresses are NOT checked against pool token immutables: wrong choices can revert, send an unexpected token or strand publicly sweepable router balances.

Amounts are raw token units, inputs uint128 constrained to signed int128 range. Every swap enforces deadline and final minimum output or maximum input; single-hop additionally applies Q64.64 marginal price limit (0 for zeroForOne open, uint128.max for opposite open). Single exact input can partially fill at its price bound. Multihop arrays must align and contain 1..256 pools; directions are bitmap bits, no per-hop price limits. Exact-output traverses pools backward through fixed internal callbacks.

extensionData is forwarded only through the selected factory pool swap to that pool's configured extension, not interpreted as arbitrary router executor calldata. Pool pricing, fees, oracle freshness, permissions, pause state and mutable configured financial hooks remain material dependencies; individual pool/hook runtime identity and configuration are not attested here.

Payable swaps may wrap native currency for the immutable wrapped-native input before transferring any remaining input from msg.sender. Excess or unspent native currency can remain on the router and is publicly refundable; ERC20-only calls should send zero native value. Fixed refund/unwrap/sweep helpers are now separately granted, but a standalone swap does not insert them or promise a full settlement workflow.

Base current Treble own Algebra Integral 1.2.2 position manager only, 0x48459abc42e5f5490169d26e1c6cc5eeb5905f07. Official current app uses this exact root. Source is a direct contract without proxy dispatch; Sourcify reports metadata-insensitive match (not exact_match) for creation/runtime, with complete applicable source and full ABI retained. No generic Algebra/fork ABI substituted.

mint/increaseLiquidity pay pool obligations from msg.sender through validated Algebra mint callback. Pool identity is deterministically derived from immutable poolDeployer and token/deployer key, not arbitrary executable calldata. Mint issues a position NFT to recipient. increaseLiquidity needs no ownership check and can donate caller funds to another owner's NFT; it does not grant control. No direct callbacks, permits, NFT approval/operator mutations, farming approvals or nonempty pool-initialization/receiver bytes are admitted. Standard NFT transfers, empty-data pool initialization and finite financial multicall are now separately granted.

Funding amounts use each underlying token's native units; liquidity uses pool liquidity units and tick range. Desired amounts bound spending and token minima/deadline constrain liquidity changes; actual liquidity may differ for fee-on-transfer tokens. Concentrated liquidity may go out of range and lose value relative to holding tokens, and fees, plugin settings, token behavior and MEV affect economics. No fixed swap fee or LP yield is promised.

decreaseLiquidity requires existing NFT owner/approval and positive liquidity, applies minima/deadline, and records principal plus earned fees as tokens owed; it does not immediately pay out. collect requires existing NFT authority, caps each token by amountMax and debt, updates fees, then pays recipient; recipient zero retains assets in the shared manager and is not a complete withdrawal. Core rounding may pay slightly less than accounted and the full expected amount is debited. burn only deletes a completely emptied position after liquidity and owed tokens are zero.

The original five selected manager lifecycle methods are payable, but native payment is wrapped only when token is WETH and manager ETH balance covers the obligation. Excess ETH is not automatically refunded; fixed sweep/refund/unwrap helpers and finite financial multicall are now separately granted. Prefer zero native value and pre-funded WETH token balances/allowance, and direct nonzero external recipients for collection; no automatic refund workflow is inserted.

Immutable factory 0x6e606cf94a4ddc01aeed2fce16d1b4f5b33e0a31, pool deployer 0x0daef94aad401c5b77aa0306f48273153752c09d and WETH 0x4200000000000000000000000000000000000006 were read at the root. Factory roles can change farming center; pre-farmed positions invoke a fixed liquidity-delta follower and failures may propagate. Pools/custom pool deployers/plugins, farming hooks, tokens and descriptor are dependencies, not independently continuously attested. Third-party aggregators, Nitro/ICHI/Gamma zaps, perps, legacy swap-retired deployment and unsupported chains are outside this inventory.

For WETH payment, pay() uses available PERIPHERY native ETH balance when sufficient, wrapping only the amount owed; this may include residual ETH, not just current msg.value. Other LP methods are nonpayable. No whole-balance wrap/sweep helper is admitted.

collect, drain, detach and portion require an actually minted LP NFT and existing owner/operator authorization through _verifyTokenIdAndGetLpNum. Receiver selects pool payout recipient.

Range edges are signed int256 values converted to tubs; portion liquidity is ABI bytes16 representing binary128 Quad, not a uint token amount. Invalid ranges, nonfinite/invalid Quad liquidity, insufficient positions or pool dependencies can revert. addLiquidity checks returned token amounts AGAINST MINIMA, not caller total-maximum-spend guards or a deadline. Exit/split methods have no explicit minimum payout or deadline. Pool pricing, fee accounting and rounding affect results; retained source does not attest every dynamic pool runtime or execution outcome.

tap is not admitted: it only decodes a caller-supplied tokenId and calls its embedded address without _requireOwned, operator authorization or factory-membership validation.
